# Independent audit: arithmetic-tail equality and rigidity

Audited `candidate 1233ee6dee49d9f8` against
`candidate 821242aee5d2f3e1`. The result passes.

1. For d>1, the positive-part functions (x+s)_+ on [0,1] are nonzero
   and pairwise nonproportional whenever distinct x,y>-1. Strict
   Minkowski therefore proves strict convexity of the increment
   function on exactly the interval required in both the initial and
   barrier triples. In particular, the initial argument remains valid
   when its parameter t lies below one.
2. The equality barrier has the claimed strict sign on each side of
   its root. Strict convexity upgrades its propagation inequality to
   a strict one, and all shifted partial-sum inequalities follow.
3. For d=1, the continuous polynomial square-root formula has negative
   second derivative except at rho=1/2. This classifies every actual
   integer triple without an endpoint exception.
4. The arbitrary concave-root reduction has nonnegative termwise
   envelope deficits. Equality in their sum forces every term,
   including the terminal support position, to agree. This gives
   precisely the odd-integer suffix and no additional equality cases.
5. In the exact gap formula, the second rationalization numerator is
   (A+b)^2-8(A-b)F. Its two denominator factors are strictly positive
   under q>1 and F>b. Thus both displayed defect formulas have the
   correct signs and constants.
6. The claims about terminal blocks of equality nodes, artificial
   zero endpoints, and the mean of a full odd profile all check. The
   congruence of (N-1)(2N-1) to one modulo N excludes an integer mean
   for N>1. Positive weights on the full support make Jensen strict
   whenever the root profile has any strict interior node.
7. The tail partition integral is strictly smaller than its finite
   upper-endpoint sum, including when Jensen happens to be an equality.
   Therefore the finite integer-mean tail bound is never attained;
   the limiting sharpness statement is consistent with the strictness.

No unresolved step or correction was found.
